lines: We moved in on a Tuesday.
On Wednesday I noticed the stairs had thirteen steps, and on Thursday they had twelve.
I told myself I had miscounted.
I am a person who tells herself things.
By the second week the number had stopped changing, but the house had begun to count other things.
The windows, first, then the spoons in the drawer, then my children asleep in their beds, each night a soft, patient "one, two" from somewhere inside the walls, the way a shepherd counts at a gate.
Last night it got to three.
I stood in the hallway in my socks, listening to the quiet arithmetic move from room to room.
Then it reached the kitchen, where I was standing, and I understood with perfect calm that the house had not been counting what we had.
It had been counting what it was still missing.
"Three," it said, kindly, from just behind my left shoulder, and a door that had never been there before began, very slowly, to open.
